messages:
alex: CI push is weird — build succeeded but integration job pulls and fails with zstd error after yesterday's Dockerfile tweaks.
ci-bot: build/ci-image-job #8726 failed - push step error
maria: @alex logs?
alex: ```
failed to apply layer: zstd: invalid header
Caused by: unexpected EOF reading compressed stream
```
sam: that looks like a blob got corrupted in the registry or objectstore.
jordan: was there any registry rotation or migrate last night?
alex: no, but we did switch to a multi-stage change that reorders layers.
maria: sometimes buildkit + cache reuse can produce the same digest for different content if the blob store was partly overwritten. try `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.internal/redwood/ci-image:ci-20260316` and `regctl blob info registry.redwood.internal sha256:abcd`.
alex: ran skopeo -> reports digest sha256:abcd size 23.1MB but `docker save` locally got 22.8MB.
linda: that size mismatch is suspicious. check harbor objectstore checksum and replication logs.
sam: quick fix: `docker pull` + `docker tag` with new tag then `docker push --disable-content-trust`? Or remove the blob and re-push.
alex: don't have registry admin perms to delete blob. can someone on infra remove suspected blob sha256:abcd?
maria: I can. I'll remove blob from harbor and ask you to re-push.
ci-bot: redeploy triggered by delete: job #8730 queued
maria: blob removed.
alex: re-pushed with --no-cache --pull, push succeeded. Running integration now.
ci-bot: build/ci-image-job #8730 succeeded
alex: integration passed. Looks like the corrupted blob was the cause. Opening infra ticket to investigate harbor/objectstore flakiness and adding a CI cache-bust step.
jordan: thanks. For postmortem: include steps to detect digest vs size mismatch in CI.
alex: will draft issue and ping @eng-infra. :thumbsup:
